summary: Outlines the transition of NIC services. It is informational and describes the plan for moving how those services are provided.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC announces a planned transfer of Network Information Center services from SRI International to Government Systems Inc. It lists the new contact details and explains when registration activity would pause and resume.

subtitle: An announcement of the planned transfer of Network Information Center services.

tldr.problem: The Network Information Center's services were scheduled to move from SRI International to Government Systems Inc.
tldr.mechanism: The memo sets out the planned transfer date, continuity arrangements, new contact details, and a temporary pause in WHOIS registration changes during database transfer.
tldr.outcome: It tells DDN and Internet users how the planned service transition would affect contacts and registrations.

today: RFC 1261 is Informational. It records the planned 1991 transfer of Network Information Center services from SRI to Government Systems Inc.

sections.title: Services Moving to a New Provider
sections.content:
The Network Information Center transition from SRI International in Menlo Park to Government Systems Inc. in Chantilly was officially scheduled for October 1, 1991. The services included network and user registration, online information services, Help Desk operations, and RFC and Internet-Draft archive and distribution services.

SRI was to continue providing all NIC services and responding to user requests through September 30, 1991.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo announces a planned change in who provides NIC services. It lists the services involved and says SRI would continue handling them through September 30.

sections.title: What Users Should Expect
sections.content:
The memo says most online services were expected to appear the same after users connected to the new NIC host. The stated exceptions were due to changing from TOPS20 to SunOS; the new host was a Sun 470 SPARCserver running SunOS 4.1.

It provides a new postal address, Help Desk phone numbers and hours, fax number, network address, and root domain server address.
sections.plainLanguage: Most online services were expected to look the same, although the host computer's operating system would change. The memo gives the new contact information.

sections.title: Registration Pause During the Transfer
sections.content:
The ID (WHOIS) database was not to be changed from September 26 through September 30, 1991, and registration actions were suspended while the master database was transferred. Starting September 26, U.S. mail and fax requests were to go to GSI, while email requests continued to the HOSTMASTER and REGISTRAR mailboxes at NIC.DDN.MIL for forwarding as appropriate.

The memo says registration activities would resume on October 1, 1991.
sections.plainLanguage: Registration changes were scheduled to stop while the database moved. The RFC says they would resume when the new NIC took over.

sections.title: Status of the Memo
sections.content: RFC 1261 provides information about the planned transition and does not specify an Internet standard.
sections.plainLanguage: This is an informational transition announcement, not a technical standard.
